rv.q: It's an endearing, if unpolished, valentine to the creative process
What on earth is this show doing on Broadway? That question is confronted head-on in the peculiar and quite adorable musical called [title of show] that opened on Thursday at the Lyceum Theater.
But the show is so desperate to be loved - and yet so defiantly defensive and so oddly pleased with its success that there's no room for audiences to discover the endearing smartness for themselves.
If all this sounds claustrophobically self-indulgent, there's a reason.
[title of show] stands pathetically naked on Broadway.
This self-referential behind-the-scenes musical comedy was clever and tuneful and bursting with charm.
The show also has a great deal of passion, tons of wit, and a handful of catchy tunes.
What is appealing, however, is director Matt Lenz’s top-notch production of “[title of show].”

"'[title of show]" has a special appeal to theater junkies, and some in the audience might find some of the references and gags obscure.
